items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: And Max Gordon, the big impresario, standing in the back with me, saying, I don't know what's wrong with that gal

ctx.x: This is how impressed you get, when you make the New York scene. That's it. So these were the early struggles in New York, until you start getting a few other breaks. Village Vanguard was a break. You go in there with your own trio, and I went in there with Max Kaminsky and Freddy Moore and then I came back or either extended the engagement when Max had left with Wild Bill Davison and Freddy Moore, working off as the group -- the Lion of Trinidad, who was a calypso innovator, and writer. He wrote that tune,…

So he was there. Pearl Bailey -- I saw Pearl Bailey on that floor, she was making either $40 or $75 a week. And Max Gordon, the big impresario, standing in the back with me, saying, I don't know what's wrong with that gal, there's something I can quite figure out. You know what he figured out? He bought the Blue Angel on the East Side with a partner, and within a couple of years, he's paying Pearl Bailey $1500 a week, and she hasn't changed a bit of that act. That's what he figured out.
She came in doing the same act. He just didn't understand it. For $75 a week, he couldn't understand it.
